newsitem.title: USA: California settles with Prudential Insurance. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT 22/2]
newsitem.headline: California settles with Prudential Insurance. [CORRECTED 09:45 GMT 22/2]

text.p: The state of California Friday reached a multimillion-dollar agreement with Prudential Insurance Co. of America, settling allegations the insurer used deceptive tactics to sell life insurance.

California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said Prudential agreed to pay $15.4 million, including a $5.5 million fine and $3 million for consumer protection (corrects from "agreed to pay $15.4 million to life insurance policyholders.") The state fined the insurer another $9.5 million as part of the settlement.
The settlement resolves a two-year investigation into allegations that Prudential Insurance agents in California deceived policyholders when selling them life insurance, the commissioner said.
In December, California, along with Florida, Texas and , Massachusetts, urged a federal judge to reject a class-action settlement by Prudential, calling it unfair to consumers.

Under that settlement, reached in September, Prudential agreed to pay at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million policyholders nationwide who bought permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995.
The proposed class-action settlement could cost Prudential as much as $1.2 billion in direct expenses and could have a total value to policyholders of almost $2 billion.
A hearing to determine the fairness of the proposed settlement is scheduled to begin Monday in U.S. District Court in Newark, N.J.
Texas, Massachusetts and Florida reached separate settlements with Prudential on Thursday.

Under Florida's settlement, Prudential agreed to pay $15 million to the state and make restitution to an estimated 128,000 Floridian policyholders to settle state charges it cheated life insurance customers.

Prudential also reached separate agreements in principle to pay Massachusetts $2.4 million and to pay Texas $2 million as well as improve the restitution offer to victims of alleged deceptive sales practices.

On Thursday, the California insurance department said it was not settling and was continuing its special investigation. An insurance department spokeswoman said the state was aggressively working to get the highest return for California consumers.

Announcing the settlement, Quackenbush said, "The original settlement negotiated by the multistate task force would have resulted in only $2.3 million for California. Under the terms of settlement reached Friday, California will get $15.4 million from Prudential Insurance Co."

Prudential Chairman Arthur F. Ryan said in a statement, "The provision negotiated by Commissioner Quackenbush, including the extension of the complaint history period and the increased interest payments, will mean enhanced remedies for customers who were misled."
Prudential agreed late last week to pay $384,200 to settle a lawsuit brought by Virginia. It acknowledged that some policyholders may have been misled by Prudential agents.
